sources.title: Application-Motivated, Holistic Benchmarking of a Full Quantum Computing Stack
evidence_supported: The paper proposes three application-motivated circuit classes: deep, shallow, and square.
The benchmark measures full-stack behavior across device and compilation choices rather than characterizing only an isolated hardware component.
The reported experiments use IBM Quantum systems and compare compilation strategies including tket and Qiskit workflows.
The paper reports that device connectivity, noise levels, and compilation strategy materially affect measured performance.
The benchmark requires classical processing and repeated samples in addition to quantum-device execution.

sources.title: Application-Motivated, Holistic Benchmarking of a Full Quantum Computing Stack
evidence_supported: The public preprint predates the 2021 peer-reviewed publication.
The preprint already describes the three application-motivated benchmark classes and empirical study on IBM Quantum systems.
The first-submission timestamp is a public disclosure proxy and does not establish the internal benchmark-framework generation date.

candidate_generation_date.rationale: The arXiv timestamp establishes public disclosure of the benchmark framework, not when the framework or experiments were first generated internally.

verification_date.rationale: Repeated hardware executions, compiler comparisons, classical scoring, and publication review are distinct validation surfaces. Current evidence does not support one canonical verification date.

technology_dependency.rationale: The benchmark is explicitly intended to characterize full quantum computing systems by running application-motivated circuits on available quantum devices, while also depending on classical compilation, sampling, and scoring.

orientation.rationale: The work evaluates the performance of quantum computing systems themselves rather than reporting an external scientific discovery enabled by quantum computation.

classes.name: deep
classes.application_motivation: state preparation relevant to variational quantum eigensolver workflows

classes.name: shallow
classes.application_motivation: IQP-type circuits relevant to near-term quantum machine learning

classes.name: square
classes.application_motivation: circuit shape inspired by quantum-volume-style benchmarking

notes: The seed candidate-generation month is preserved as a preprint proxy and not silently converted to an internal generation date.
The seed publication date is supported by the primary journal record.

remaining_questions: Recover exact experimental run dates and device-specific execution metadata where primary archives permit.
Code downstream adoption, replication, benchmark reuse, and supersession as separate events rather than inferring recognition from publication.
Separate benchmark-framework formulation from individual hardware execution and compiler-comparison events if later tranche-02 analysis requires it.
Assess later full-stack benchmark use across independent platforms without treating citation alone as adoption evidence.
